feedback: No race evidence exists yet: this is iteration 0 and the Builder's baseline has never raced, so every claim below is a reasoned expectation, not a measurement. Compensation I had to make: the sensor weights are scaled from lateral position (x/0.012, clipped to [-2, 2]) because the five sensors span only 0.048 m, and the 12 mm footprint means adjacent sensors overlap the tape together. Controller choices that depend on geometry: kp=3 and kd=0.3 were set because the 0.12 m track and 0.8 kg mass give moderate yaw authority. If the next race (iteration 0 results) shows steering_oscillation high or max_error rising on bends, then the forward offset is too large or the sensors respond too late: reduce sensor y from 0.04 toward 0.02 and reduce the track to 0.10 m so the turn response is quicker. If line_loss_events are high on the tight bends (the robot leaves the tape at the edge of the 0.048 m spread), then widen the spread to about 0.064 m (x of ±0.032 is outside the allowed range, so use ±0.030 with 5 sensors) to see the line for longer. If completion_time is over 3 s with no oscillation or loss, then reduce mass toward 0.6 kg to speed acceleration, since the controller can keep base speed at 1.6 without extra correction.
requested_changes: If steering_oscillation is high in the next race, move all sensor y values from 0.04 to 0.02 (forward offset down) and keep the rest fixed, because a sensor closer to the axle reacts later and reduces the overshoot the controller must damp.

If line_loss_events are high on tight bends, widen the sensor lateral spread to x = ±0.030 (about 0.06 m total span) in place of ±0.024, since the baseline 0.048 m span loses the tape when the line drifts at the edge of the sensor array.
If completion_time exceeds 3 s without line loss, reduce mass from 0.8 to 0.6 kg, since lower yaw inertia and mass should let the robot reach the 1.5 m/s average speed sooner.
